description: pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:328-347: rank_candidates allocates Vec<(u8, usize)> with capacity == pool.len(), then sorts. Called once per frame; per Frame.ranked = Some(ranked). For typical PKI (small pools, shallow chains) this is one or two small allocations per build_path call. For a build_first_valid_path loop that iterates many candidates in a large pool, the allocation cost compounds: every backtrack to a frame re-uses the cached ranked Vec (fine), but every NEW frame allocates. Not in a hot path that anyone has measured. Flag for the case where the pool grows to thousands of certs (federal bridge PKI scenarios). Alternative shape: a two-pass scan that yields candidates lazily by tier. Probably not worth the complexity unless profiling shows it.
title: rank_candidates allocates Vec per frame even for one-candidate matches; consider iterator-based ranking for hot DFS path
